prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Green Party Manifesto 2005 — Summary (under 500 words)

Vision
- Build a sustainable society based on social, economic and environmental justice. Reverse privatisation of public services, cut inequality, and tackle climate change with long-term policies.

Economy
- Reduce inequality via more progressive income tax (50% over £50k; 60% over £100k), more bands in Corporation Tax (up to 40% for largest firms), higher taxes on unearned wealth, inheritance taxed by recipient.
- Abolish National Insurance, shift burden to comprehensive income taxes.
- Pilot Land Value Tax set by local authorities to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates.
- Replace VAT with revenue-neutral eco-taxes tied to resource use, pollution and waste.
- Support small businesses, remove employers’ NIC, and promote community banks, credit unions and local currencies.
- Oppose UK entry to the euro; reform WTO; measure wellbeing beyond GDP (ISEW/MDP).
- Defend workers’ rights and reduce working hours.

Energy & Climate
- Adopt Contraction and Convergence: CO2 cuts of 20% by 2010, 50% by 2020, 85% by 2030.
- Introduce a Carbon Tax based on fuel carbon content; protect low-use households by reforming tariffs.
- Generate 40% of energy from renewables by 2020; redirect nuclear subsidies to renewables; scale solar, wind, wave and biogas.
- Cut demand via a Warmer Homes Act and “Smart Energy Councils”; close nuclear programme at end of plant life; Cabinet post for climate policy.

Welfare
- Phase in a universal, non-means-tested Citizen’s Income replacing most benefits; retain/add specialist benefits; integrate housing support later.
- Introduce a universal Citizen’s Pension linked to earnings, replacing Pension Credit.
- Simplify child benefits; expand Sure Start; reduce maximum working week and explore 35-hour average.
- Boost affordable housing: allow councils to reinvest receipts, support co-ops, LVT reform, and energy-efficiency upgrades.

Health & Education
- Restore NHS principles; end PPPs and marketisation; increase prevention and mental health focus.
- Abolish prescription charges; reinstate free eye tests and dental care; expand access to holistic treatments.
- Raise health funding to at least 9% of GNP; consider hypothecated NHS Tax; redirect future defence savings.
- Increase education funding, especially early years and post-16; scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; abolish SATs; move toward Individual Learning Plans.

Transport
- Prioritise walking, cycling, public transport; target 10% road traffic reduction by 2010; shift £30bn from roads to public transit; re-regulate buses.
- Return rail and Tube to public ownership; expand rail and light rail; boost rail freight.
- Internalise motoring costs via congestion/road pricing, higher fuel duty, freight levies; support R&D for efficient vehicles.
- Resist airport expansion; ban night flights; tax aviation (EU fuel tax; UK emissions tax for domestic flights); raise passenger duty.

Environment
- Zero Waste Strategy: outlaw incineration, cut packaging, set recycled content standards; 60% household recycling by 2010; create a Zero Waste Agency.
- Establish an Environmental Protection Commission; strengthen chemicals regulation; levy eco-taxes on polluting inputs.
- Apply precautionary principle to GM, xenotransplantation and nanotech; oppose patents on natural resources.
- Strengthen animal welfare: end live exports; ban battery cages (incl. enriched), tighten broiler standards; ban fur imports.

Food & Farming
- Organics Target Bill: 30% organic production by 2012; support local markets, co-ops and farm schemes.
- Replace CAP/CFP with policies for localisation, biodiversity and sustainable incomes.
- Ban GM food; toughen supermarket Code of Practice and oversight of mergers.

Crime & Justice
- Focus on prevention via urban design, youth facilities, rapid repairs, staffed public spaces; treat drug use primarily as a health issue; oppose ID cards.
- Expand community policing, local stations and oversight; restore social “guardians.”
- Tighten gun laws (clear lethality thresholds, broad prohibitions, single robust licensing).
- Embed restorative justice; strengthen human rights, tackle hate crime and violence against women; support a strong disability directive.

Democracy
- Oppose national ID cards and biometric database.
- Renew local government with stronger powers, LVT, PR voting, citizen-initiated referenda and recall.
- PR for Westminster; elected House of Lords.
- Regional devolution in England; more powers for Scotland/Wales if supported.
- Draft a written constitution; disestablish the Church of England.

Peace & International
- Ethical foreign policy: withdraw from Iraq in favour of UN peacekeepers; reduce defence to EU average; decommission nuclear weapons; end arms export support; pursue an Arms Trade Treaty.
- Increase aid to at least 1% of GNI; cancel debts of the 52 poorest countries; back a Tobin tax; reform carbon trading to aid the Global South.
- Reform UN Security Council (end permanent vetoes); democratise IMF/World Bank.
- Oppose proposed EU constitution but support EU reform for democracy and sustainability.
- Replace/reshape WTO with a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade (GAST) to permit localisation and fair trade.
- Uphold rights of asylum seekers (to work, fair appeals), ratify migrant worker conventions, and improve procedures.
